text.p: President Clinton and his wife Hillary had adjusted gross income of $1,065,101 in 1996, including his $200,000 salary and $742,852 in royalties from her book "It Takes A Village," the White House said on Monday.

The earnings represent a huge jump from the previous year, when the Clintons had an adjusted gross income of $316,074. The couple paid $199,791 in federal income tax for 1996, up from $75,437 the previous year.

All income from Hillary Clinton's book, net of taxes and administrative expenses, were donated to charity, representing the bulk of the $609,300 in charitable deductions reported in the Clintons' income tax return released by the White House.

The return, signed by both Clintons and dated April 14, 1997, also showed a capital gain of $100,066 from the Boston Harbor Trust Co., taxable interest income of $28,606, dividend income of $5,141 and $2,214 in income attributed to taxable refunds, credits or offsets of state and local income taxes. Boston Harbor is the trustee of the Clintons' blind trust.
The White House said Clinton also filed a federal income tax return for Chelsea Clinton, his 17-year-old daughter, which showed income of $13,101 and tax of $1,969.

According to the documents released by the White House, Clinton and his wife were due a $5,876 refund for 1996, which they have chosen to apply to their 1997 taxes. The refund was the result of their having paid $205,667 in federal taxes, an overpayment when compared to the $199,791 they actually owed.
